definitions.hash_discrepancy_explanation: The two hashes above are the SAME pinned-commit file, verified identical logical content: WoWDBDefs has no .gitattributes controlling line endings, so Git on Windows checked the file out with CRLF while our Linux checkout kept LF. Converting the LF copy's line endings to CRLF byte-for-byte reproduces the Windows hash exactly (independently confirmed). This is a known, explained, cosmetic difference -- not a content mismatch, tampering, or wrong-commit issue.

notes: Build Key and CDN Key for wow_classic_beta / 1.60.1.69913 in this operator's .build.info exactly match the archived Blizzard CDN record for the same build in mdX7/ribbit_data (v2/products/wow_classic_beta/version-wow_classic_beta-4026306.bmime, US region), independently recorded during the M1.5 research pass (see forever-db/research/m1_5/build_identity.json). This install also has four other products (wow_classic_era 1.15.9.69722, wow_classic 5.5.4.69585, wow_anniversary 2.5.6.69795, retail wow 12.1.0.69875), all sharing the same CDN Key except retail, which has its own KeyRing populated — noted for context, not analyzed further here. Executable's own embedded version resource (compiled in by Blizzard, distinct from the Battle.net-agent-written .build.info) independently reads FileVersion=1.60.1.69913, matching .build.info and the archived CDN record exactly. Three independent sources now agree on this build identity: archived third-party CDN record [2nd], .build.info [V, agent-written cache], executable version resource [V, compiled into the binary]. This is still not a live Blizzard confirmation from this pipeline, but it is strong convergent evidence. File on disk is WowB.exe; its OriginalFilename resource field says WoW.exe, consistent with Battle.net renaming a shared client binary per-flavor to avoid filename collisions across the five installed products, not a distinct program. /dump GetBuildInfo() in-game confirms build 69913 a fourth independent way (archived CDN record [2nd], .build.info [V], exe version resource [V], live API call [V] -- all four agree). Interface version 16001 falls in the 16000-16999 range that lodestar's notes (M1.5 research, tagged [2nd] there) claimed identifies Forever as running on the interface-range used by the modern/retail client rather than Era's. That specific claim is now upgraded to [V] on this real client. GetBuildInfo() returned two extra values ([5]='' , [6]=' ') beyond the documented 4-tuple (version, build, date, tocversion) -- their meaning is unconfirmed; not guessing further. Build config file at Data/config/6c/0d/6c0df97e... (content-addressed) verified by the operator: MD5 of its content EQUALS the Build Key from .build.info (case-insensitive match), and its own 'build-name' field reads 'WOW-69913patch1.60.1_ForeverBeta' -- a Blizzard-build-system-authored, tamper-evident label naming this exact build and patch as the Forever beta. Five independent things now agree on build identity: archived CDN record [2nd], .build.info [V], exe version resource [V], live GetBuildInfo() [V], and this content-addressed build config's own build-name field [V]. This is the strongest evidence obtainable without a live query to Blizzard's version service, which remains undone. root/encoding hashes recorded (f529ea6a... / 6cee0cc1...) for use by the extraction tool in the next step. [FINDING] Real client header_record_count is 6690, not the 6600 reported by ForeverDiff and lodestar's docs (M1.5 research, both [2nd]). The unencrypted section (section 0) contains EXACTLY 6600 records, matching those sources precisely. Two further sections (11 and 79 records, 90 total) are flagged encrypted (nonzero TactKeyLookup) and were not read (no TACT keys used, per operator instruction). Strong evidence that prior [2nd] row-count claims reflected only the unencrypted portion of QuestV2 and did not disclose the existence of 90 additional encrypted records. [NOTE, uninterpreted] schema_string reads 'WOWSTATIC_1_60_1_69800', a build number not matching any of 69876/69893/69913. [V] that the file contains this string; [?] whether it marks the build where this table's layout was last established (most likely) vs something else -- not confirmed, and does not contradict the five-way build-identity confirmation already on record for 1.60.1.69913.
